editorial:
Imagine feeling like a ghost in your own house, doing everything for a husband who doesn't even respect you. That is exactly where you find the main character in this story. She is a typical housewife who has put her own dreams on hold, only to deal with her husband's constant cheating. The movie feels very real and relatable, showing that slow burn of frustration that happens when you realize you deserve more. When she finally snaps and heads back to grad school, the whole mood changes. You get to see her meet a group of bold, loud, and smart women who push her to stop apologizing for existing and start speaking her mind.

The acting is top-notch and makes you really feel the emotional weight of her journey. While the pace is a bit slower than a modern thriller, it lets the character growth feel natural. You might find some of the 1980s dialogue a bit dated, but the message of finding yourself still hits home today. If you want to see it, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best quality. It is a great pick if you love stories about personal growth and breaking free from toxic relationships.
endingExplained: In the end, the main character finally stops letting her husband control her life. She realizes that she cannot go back to being the quiet, obedient wife she used to be. After finding her strength and confidence through her studies and her new friends, she chooses her own happiness over a broken marriage. She leaves the toxic relationship behind for good, walking away with a new sense of identity and a bright future ahead of her.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about finding independence and personal growth.
